simple.meaning: לָכַד (lâkad) appears 121 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship and in connection with priesthood.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, and 12 more, beginning at Numbers 21:32. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship, priesthood, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לָכַד (H3920) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows לָכַד through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

definitions.full: H3920. lakad לָכַד 121 verb capture, seize, take (by lot) (Phoenician לכד take out, choose (?); לְכַד ᵑ7 as Biblical Hebrew; Arabic is strike, push , with the hand, etc., pestle , compare modern attack Wetzst ZMG xxii. 1868, 140 ; stick or cleave to); — Qal Perfect ׳ל Josh 8:1 +, לָכַדְתִּי 2Sam 12:27 etc.; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִלְכּוֺד Amos 3:5 ; וַיִּלְכֹּד Judg 8:12 +, etc.; Imperative masculine singular suffix לָכְדָהּ 2Sam 12:28 , masculine plural לִכְדוּ ; Infinitive absolute לָכוֺד Amos 3:5 ; construct suffix לְלָכְדֵנִי Jer 18:22 , לְלָכְדָהּ 32:24 ; Participle לֹכֵד Job 5:13 ; Prov 16:32 ; — 1 capture, seize (not in P) with accusative, usually a city or town, in war Judg 1:8 , 12 ; Josh 8:21 ; 10:1 (JE), Deut 2:35 48t. (but Judg 1:18 strike out as gloss Bu Kit GFM and others); land Josh 10:42 (D), Dan 11:18 ; water-courses (fords), Judg 3:28 ; 7:24 (twice in verse); 12:8 ; object men (usually princes, kings) in battle 7:25 ; 8:12 , 14 ; Josh 11:12 , 17 (D), 2Chr 22:9 ; 33:11 ; captives and spoils 2Sam 8:4 = 1Chr 18:4 ; of Saul's seizing the kingdom ( הַמְּלוּכָה ), i.e. acquiring it actually by force of arms 1Sam 14:47 ; also of Samson's catching the foxes Judg 15:4 ; of a lion catching his prey Amos 3:4 ; of a trap, snare, יִלְכּוֺד לָכוֺד 3:5 . 2 figurative of entrapping men Jer 5:26 ; Psa 35:8 , compare Prov 5:22 ; Job 5:13 and (of a pit) Jer 18:22 . 3 of taking by lot Josh 7:14 (3 t. in verse); 7:17 (J E; see Niph`al 3 ). Niph`al Perfect נִלְכַּד Lam 4:20 ; 3 feminine singular נִלְכְּדָה 1Kin 16:18 +, etc.; Imperfect יִלָּכֵד Isa 24:18 ; Jer 48:44 ; כָּהּ יִלָּ֫כֶד Eccl 7:26 ; וַיִּלָּכֵד Josh 7:16 +, etc.; Participle נִלְכָּד 7:15 ; — 1 be captured in war, of city 1Kin 16:18 ; 2Kin 18:10 ; Jer 38:28 (twice in verse); 48:1 , 41 ; 50:2 , 9 , 24 ; 51:31 , 41 ; Zech 14:2 ; of men Jer 51:56 ; Lam 4:20 (compare Qal 1 ). 2 of men, be caught , namely, in a snare or trap, only figurative, usually by divine judgment Isa 8:15 ; 24:18 ; 28:13 ; Psa 9:16 ; 59:13 ; Prov 6:2 ; 11:6 ; Jer 6:11 ; 8:9 ; so of Moab 48:7 , 44 ; of being ensnared by a woman Eccl 7:26 ; of being caught by cords of distress, עֹ֑נִי בְּחַבְלֵי , Job 36:8 . 3 be taken by lot Josh 7:15-16 , 17 , 18 (all J E), 1Sam 10:20-21 , (twice in verse); 14:41-42 , (compare Qal 3 ). Let a cry be heard from their houses
For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, “Why do you prophesy, and say, ‘Yahweh says, “Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will take it;

“Behold, siege ramps have come to the city to take it. The city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans who fight against it, because of the sword, of the famine, and of the pestilence. What you have spoken has happened. Behold, you see it.
Therefore Yahweh says: Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will take it.

Behold, I will command,” says Yahweh, “and cause them to return to this city. They will fight against it, take it, and burn it with fire. I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.”
The Chaldeans will come again, and fight against this city. They will take it and burn it with fire.” ’
